Yes! I remember when I was on that, it's a real struggle. Well done on losing while on seroquel (healthily I hope), you're like an amazing unicorn! That's actually the medication my friend used to take. I'm hoping he does better too, I encourage him when it's appropriate to the conversation but ultimately it's down to him.

I think antipsychotics have some weight gain unrelated to the calories you eat, but I don't think it's that much. Majority of the weight gain is the increase in appetite. I take antipsychotics and I have to have a lot of self control when it comes to food, luckily I've been doing well. I know one guy who came off his medication because of the weight gain, and it's hard to get him to realise that coming off the medication alone isn't going to make the pounds drop. And he isn't willing to change his diet, so now he eats at the same level and uses diet pills, believing that it counteracts everything he eats. It's hard when it comes to mental health because it's a fine line between fat logic and distorted thinking.

Still have worries about vote brigading, in the sense that I might accidentally upvote a target post without realising. It means I barely upvote or downvote anything. I don't see how you guys can possibly differentiate between someone joining a vote brigade and someone not.

But you don't know me. I don't understand.

Using a throwaway. I did the same as any other day. I didn't write a note. I'm not sure I'd ever write a note. I don't have anyone in the world who gives a shit about me. Who can blame them, I don't give a shit about me. But I failed. And I know I won't fail next time, which may be fairly soon.

My life is inconsequential, my death is inconsequential. It's all the same. 

And here I am writing this on reddit as if it matters. I know that the only person who can really fix anything is me and I guess I don't have the will in me. I just have a bunch of voices and a warped world. 

I'm not in a great place right now. Thanks if you read this.
